title: Adaptive Prefill Interleaver and Kernel Synthesizer for Low-Percentile Latency
creator: Marta Chen
description: Reduce 95th/99th token latency in mixed-workload serving by reordering prefill work and biasing kernel selection toward shapes that minimize stall amplification. Deliver a low-risk, incremental deployable that integrates with existing admission controls and kernel hints.
background: We observe sporadic 95th+ token latency spikes on mixed-length workloads. Root causes include small numbers of long-prefill requests causing kernel-context switches, attention matrix layouts that defeat the preferred kernel for contiguous batches, and adversarial arrival patterns that force suboptimal kernel choice during decode. Existing batching and admission systems focus on slot-level fairness but don't restructure the prefill queue to produce kernel-friendly coalesces. This ticket implements an interleaver to reshape prefill ordering and a lightweight "kernel synthesizer" to smooth kernel transitions at runtime.
proposal: 1) Prefill Interleaver: a scheduler layer that groups waiting prefill tasks into micro-windows (10-50ms) and emits an interleaved stream prioritizing kernel-friendly shape combinations (e.g., merge two short-first-prefill with one long to hit batch height thresholds). 2) Kernel Synthesizer: a probabilistic selector that blends kernel assignment decisions across a short horizon to avoid flip-flopping (soft affinity + decay). 3) Decode alignment: schedule decode work so that prefill→decode handoffs preserve KV-cache locality and reduce kernel warmup. 4) Integrations: expose tuning knobs per-customer (latency_budget_ms, kernel_smoothness) and fallbacks to strict admission when load dictates.
design_decisions: Micro-window size chosen as 20ms default to balance batching vs latency; made configurable per-tenant.
Use probabilistic kernel synth (exponential decay) instead of hard pinning to allow graceful fallback under capacity pressure.
Keep interleaver stateless across scheduling epochs to avoid complex rollback logic during node failures.
Prefer conservative defaults that preserve existing SLOs; aggressive smoothing behind feature flag for experimental runs.
experiments: Testbed: 4x A100, mixed workload: 60% short (prefill 8-64 tokens), 30% med (128-512), 10% long (1k-2k).
Baselines: current admission + kernel picker (runtime-1.18). Collect p50/p95/p99 token latencies and decode throughput.
Experiment A: Enable interleaver only; measure effect on 95/99 latency and overall throughput.
Experiment B: Enable kernel synthesizer only; measure kernel switch frequency and tail latency.
Experiment C: Interleaver + synthesizer + decode alignment with conservative knobs; test across 0.5x, 1x, 2x offered load.
Success criteria: p95 token latency reduction >=20% and p99 reduction >=15% without >3% throughput regression at nominal load.
perf_results: Preliminary run (canary env) - nominal load: baseline p95=210ms, p99=420ms; interleaver+p-synth yielded p95=162ms (-23%), p99=350ms (-16%).
Throughput impact: measured -1.8% effective tokens/sec at nominal due to slightly larger micro-batches; within target.
Kernel switch frequency reduced by ~36% in med/long mixtures which correlated with reduced decode stalls.
Worst-case under 2x load: p99 still improves but throughput drops ~5% — we gate aggressive knobs behind traffic-aware fallback.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: enable for 1% of hosted API traffic with telemetry validation (2 weeks).
Canary: dedicated Dedicated cluster canary for customers on runtime-1.20 internal pool for 72h run.
Gradual ramp if key metrics stable: 1%→5%→20%→100% over 4 weeks with automated rollback on thresholds.
Fallback paths: revert to strict admission (no interleaver) if kernel-synth causes >10% p99 regression or error rate up.
telemetry: New metrics: interleaver_emit_rate, avg_micro_window_ms, kernel_switch_rate_1m, synth_confidence_score, prefill_to_decode_handshake_latency.
Alerts: increase in kernel_switch_rate_1m > 2x baseline or p99_token_latency regression > 10% triggers rollback runbook.
Add trace tags for interleaver_id and synth_decision to correlate with distributed traces and flamegraphs.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Interleaver could increase average latency for ultra-low-latency customers. Mitigation: per-tenant latency_budget_ms default to 0 (no interleave) unless opted-in.
Risk: Kernel synth introduces suboptimal kernel affinity causing throughput drop. Mitigation: decay parameter tune + safety net that reverts to kernel with best historical throughput.
Risk: Complexity in prefill→decode handoff. Mitigation: keep handshake protocol unchanged; only reorder queue entries visible to scheduler.
